message.content: The viscous friction force depends on two key parameters: the damping coefficient and the velocity of the oscillating body. Body velocity distinguishes this linear resistive force from all other types of friction. Friction of this viscous nature must be included in the physical pendulum model whenever the pendulum swings within a fluid medium such as air or liquid. Liquid or gaseous resistance causes the oscillation amplitude to decay progressively over time. Time-dependent energy dissipation is the main reason the damping term is added to the pendulum equation. Equation solutions that omit this term predict perpetual oscillation, which is physically unrealistic. Unrealistic predictions arise precisely when real-world viscous effects are ignored in the model.
